title: 2025-06 QBR / Health Check - Nimbus Data
summary: Quarterly business review covering usage trends, cost optimization opportunities, recent reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment for Nimbus's inference workloads on Redwood.
next_steps: Samantha Lee - send detailed cost breakdown and savings plan by 2025-06-20
Ravi Patel - propose batch/quantization config and run sample benchmark with Nimbus data by 2025-06-27
Nimbus (Aisha) - schedule Dedicated pilot week of 2025-06-30
Jordan Kim - share roadmap items and SOC2 gap doc by 2025-06-22
action_items: Samantha Lee | Send updated pricing spreadsheet | 2025-06-20
Ravi Patel | Run quantization benchmark and share results | 2025-06-27
Aisha Khan (Nimbus) | Provide production prompt set and sample logs | 2025-06-24
transcript:
[00:00] Samantha Lee: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, we're gonna run through the qbr and a quick health check. we'll keep this to about 40 minutes and then open for questions. um quick roll call?
[00:08] Aisha Khan: hey, aisha here from nimbus, thanks Sam.
[00:11] Mark Redd: Mark from platform, good to be here.
[00:14] Priya Shah: Priya, finance — hi all.
[00:17] Samantha Lee: awesome. ravi, jordan you on?
[00:19] Ravi Patel: yep ravi on the call, se. morning.
[00:22] Jordan Kim: jordan, csm, thanks.
[00:25] Samantha Lee: cool, first slide — usage and cost. for the quarter your monthly token volume has grown ~38% q/q, with peak qps during batch jobs on weekdays between 10 and 14utc, right? is that consistent with what you see, mark?
[00:40] Mark Redd: yeah that's right, we see those spikes. um one nuance — about half of those requests are from nightly ingestion pipelines so latency isn't super critical, but the chat surface needs sub 200ms p95.
[00:52] Samantha Lee: got it, that's helpful. so overall cost this quarter is up ~42% driven by model size selection and unbatched short calls. priya, i know finance wanted the cost per inference number — we're showing an effective per-1k-token cost of $3.20 on hosted, could be cut to around $1.80 with dedicated + quantization for the non-latency-sensitive pipelines.
[01:14] Priya Shah: okay that delta is huge — i need to see the breakdown. do those savings include expected infra fees for dedicated?
[01:20] Samantha Lee: yes includes reserved capacity pricing, amortized infra and a conservative estimate for burst capacity. we'll send the spreadsheet.
[01:26] Aisha Khan: curious — what about quality tradeoffs when you quantize? our prompts are fairly long, sometimes 1.5k tokens.
[01:34] Ravi Patel: good question. quantization typically hits smaller models more, but with model-specific calibration we keep top-k behavior and outputs largely intact. for your 1.5k sequences we recommend int8 with per-layer calibration and a small eval run. we'll do a smoke test on your prompt set.
[01:48] Aisha Khan: ok that sounds sensible, would like to see the eval.
[01:51] Samantha Lee: next, reliability and incidents. you had two incidents in april and may — a regional networking flake and an autoscaling misconfig that delayed some canary rollouts. uptime overall was 99.92% for the quarter; the net impact was a handful of failed inference requests during spikes. mark, did you want to add details on the platform side?
[02:12] Mark Redd: yeah the autoscale policy we used had a very aggressive cooldown, so when we hit a sudden burst it didn't spin up fast enough. we also saw some 5xx traces linked to our ingress gateway config. we've since adjusted the cooldown and are routing a subset to a warm pool.
[02:28] Samantha Lee: thanks. we've implemented a longer warm pool retention for your reserved nodes and added a fallback to a smaller but compatible model in a different region to avoid full outage. that rollback path is configured in your account.
[02:40] Aisha Khan: that fallback is good — any data exfil risk when we failover to hosted variants? we need to keep logs on-prem.
[02:47] Jordan Kim: yes — failover respects data residency settings; logs are forwarded only to your configured retention, and we can disable certain telemetry. we also have KMS integrations for key control.
[02:56] Aisha Khan: perfect, also SOC2 stuff — audit wants details on RBAC and SSO.
[02:59] Samantha Lee: we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls; jordan will share the SOC2 gap doc and our policy artifacts after this call.
[03:08] Priya Shah: and encryption at rest?
[03:10] Ravi Patel: yes all data at rest encrypted, customer keys supported via KMS/HSM in dedicated and private deployments.
[03:16] Samantha Lee: moving on — roadmap alignment. we heard you wanted better cost visibility per route and token-level breakdowns. we have a console beta for per-route token cost that you can opt into — jordan, can you speak to rollout timeline?
[03:29] Jordan Kim: it's currently in beta for a handful of customers; we'll enable Nimbus next week. it surfaces token counts, model selection, and delta cost per route. feedback loop is quick so we can add a csv export for finance.
[03:39] Priya Shah: csv export would be ideal.
[03:41] Samantha Lee: noted. other feature asks — Aisha mentioned deterministic replay for debug, and improved KV cache visibility. both are on the product backlog; we can prioritize if they're major blockers for the pilot.
[03:54] Aisha Khan: deterministic replay is important for our MLOps debugging, yes.
[03:58] Samantha Lee: great. quick touch on dedicated vs hosted — our recommendation: move ingestion/batch pipelines to Dedicated with quantization and caching to get the immediate cost wins; keep chat/low-latency pathways on Hosted or Dedicated with pinned low-latency pool, depending on your SLO and budget. does that align with internal plans?
[04:19] Mark Redd: aligns. we want a hybrid approach. main concern is procurement timeline and contract terms.
[04:25] Samantha Lee: procurement — we can start with a short pilot commit to Reserved capacity and instrument savings expectations; procurement usually needs 4-6 weeks. priya, any timeline constraints?
[04:35] Priya Shah: finance wants Q3 approval, so making the business case in next two weeks helps.
[04:40] Samantha Lee: understood, we'll prioritize sending the cost model.
[04:44] Aisha Khan: also wanted to ask about integrations — does Redwood support private deployment in our vpc? we've got compliance constraints for PHI.
[04:52] Ravi Patel: yes, private deployment in VPC or on-prem option is available; onboarding time is longer but supports HSM and stricter network controls. we'll share a checklist.
[05:01] Samantha Lee: ok open Q&A — Mark: any recommendations for mitigating transient 5xx during spike?
[05:07] Ravi Patel: we suggest a two-tier cache: prefix caching for repeated prompts plus a warm pool and request-level circuit breaker; also set a graceful fallback policy to the smaller model we discussed.
[05:18] Mark Redd: sounds good, we'll try the warm pool change.
[05:21] Samantha Lee: action items recap: we'll send the cost breakdown and a suggested reserved capacity number, ravi will run a quantization bench on your prompt set, jordan will share SOC2 artifacts and roadmap notes. Aisha, you'll provide sample prompts and logs. is that accurate?
[05:35] Aisha Khan: yes that's right — i'll get the prompts over by tuesday.
[05:39] Priya Shah: i'll need the spreadsheet to present to budget committee.
[05:42] Samantha Lee: we'll target sending the materials by end of day friday, 6/20. any blockers?
[05:48] Aisha Khan: none from us.
[05:50] Jordan Kim: i'll enable the per-route beta and send the invite.
[05:54] Samantha Lee: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in the crm with links. any final questions?
[06:00] Mark Redd: nope, thanks.
[06:02] Priya Shah: thanks all.
[06:04] Samantha Lee: thanks, bye.
[06:06] [call ends]
